correctness.rationale: The ordered magnitudes have density 2f(p)f(u), the reinforcing-sign event has probability 1/2, and the exact Schur complement splits the event according to the maximum original entry. Two rescaled two-deficit simplices each contribute J/2, while the three-deficit pivot-max region is O(epsilon^3). A Gaussian integral evaluates J=1/(2*pi^2). The standard-library verifier tests the algebra on independent samples; experiments are not the proof.

value.rationale: Two-by-two GEPP is the smallest natural setting in which Wilkinson growth can occur, so its exact Gaussian mass near the extremal face is a motivated canonical invariant. The exact quadratic exponent and 1/(2*pi^2) coefficient are not obtained from the deterministic maximum and supply a benchmark for rare-event simulation and future higher-dimensional local analysis without asserting any such extension.
